A cubical block of density $\rho_{b} = 600\ \mathrm{kg/m^{3}}$ floats in a liquid of density $\rho_{e} = 900\ \mathrm{kg/m^{3}}$. If the height of block is H = 8.0 cm then height of the submerged part is ________ cm.
questions.solution:
For a floating object :
$\frac{\text{Volume submerged}}{\text{Total Volume}} = \frac{\rho_{solid}}{\rho_{Liquid}}$
$\frac{AH_{Submerged}}{AH} = \frac{600}{900} = \frac{2}{3}$
$H_{submerged} = \frac{2}{3}H = 5.3\ \mathrm{cm}$

questions.stem: Distance between an object and three times magnified real image is 40 cm. The focal length of the mirror used is _________ cm.
questions.solution:
Real Image $\Rightarrow$ Concave mirror
$\because m = 3 \Rightarrow \frac{|v|}{|u|} = 3 \Rightarrow |v| = 3|u|$ & $|v| - |u| = 40$
$\therefore |u| = 20\ \mathrm{cm}$ & $|v| = 60\ \mathrm{cm}$
$\frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{P} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{-60} + \frac{1}{-20} = \frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow f = -15\ \mathrm{cm}$

questions.stem: 10 mole of an ideal gas is undergoing the process shown in the figure. The heat involved in the process from $P_{1}$ to $P_{2}$ to $\alpha$ Joule ($P_{1} = 21.7\ \mathrm{Pa}$ and $P_{2} = 30\ \mathrm{Pa}$, $C_{v} = 21\ \mathrm{J/K.mol}$, $R = 8.3\ \mathrm{J/mol.K}$). The value of $\alpha$ is
questions.solution:
$Q = nC_{v}\Delta T$
$\therefore v = \text{const.} \Rightarrow V\Delta P = nR\Delta T \Rightarrow \Delta T = \frac{V\Delta P}{nR}$
$\therefore Q = nC_{v}\left[\frac{V\Delta P}{nR}\right] = \frac{C_{v}V\Delta P}{R} = 21$

questions.stem: Five persons $P_{1}$, $P_{2}$, $P_{3}$, $P_{4}$ and $P_{5}$ recorded object distance ($u$) and image distance ($v$) using same convex lens having power +5 D as (25,96), (30,62), (35,37), (45,35) and (50,32) respectively. Identify correct statement
questions.solution:
$P = +5D = \frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow f = 0.2\ \mathrm{m} = 20\ \mathrm{cm}$
Leus formula : $\frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u} = \frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{20}$
$P_{1} : \frac{1}{96} - \frac{1}{-25} = \frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow f = 19.83\ \mathrm{cm}$
$P_{2} : \frac{1}{62} - \frac{1}{-30} = \frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow f = 20.21\ \mathrm{cm}$
$P_{3} : \frac{1}{37} - \frac{1}{-35} = \frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow f = 17.99\ \mathrm{cm}$
$P_{4} : \frac{1}{35} - \frac{1}{-45} = \frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow f = 19.69\ \mathrm{cm}$
$P_{5} : \frac{1}{50} - \frac{1}{-32} = \frac{1}{f} \Rightarrow f = 19.51\ \mathrm{cm}$
Among all, $P_{3}$ is way off.

options.text: Readings recorded by $P_{4}$ and $P_{5}$ persons are incorrect
Readings recorded by $P_{3}$ person are incorrect
Readings recorded by $P_{3}$ and $P_{2}$ persons are incorrect
Readings recorded by all persons are correct

The binding energy for the following nuclear reactions are expressed in MeV.
$\mathrm{{}_{2}He^{3} + {}_{0}n^{1} \rightarrow {}_{2}He^{4} + 20\,MeV}$
$\mathrm{{}_{2}He^{4} + {}_{0}n^{1} \rightarrow {}_{2}He^{5} - 0.9\,MeV}$
If $X_{3}, X_{4}, X_{5}$ denote the stability of $\mathrm{{}_{2}He^{3}}$, $\mathrm{{}_{2}He^{4}}$ and $\mathrm{{}_{2}He^{5}}$, respectively, then the correct order is :
questions.solution:
More energy is released in formation of $\mathrm{{}_{2}He^{4}}$ by $\mathrm{{}_{2}He^{3}}$
$\therefore x_{4}$ is highest.
Also, small energy is released in formation of $\mathrm{{}_{2}He^{4}}$ by $\mathrm{{}_{2}He^{5}}$
$\therefore x_{4} > x_{5} > x_{3}$

questions.stem:
In case of vertical circular motion of a particle by a thread of length r if the tension in the thread is zero at an angle $30^\circ$ shown in figure, the velocity at the bottom point (A) of the circular path is
(gravitational acceleration)
questions.solution:
for T = 0, $mg\cos 60^\circ = \frac{mv^{2}}{r}$
$\therefore \frac{1}{2}mv^{2} = \frac{mgr}{4}$
By energy conservation.
$\frac{1}{2}mu^{2} = \frac{1}{2}mv^{2} + mg\left(r + \frac{r}{2}\right)$
$= \frac{mgr}{4} + \frac{3}{2}mgr \Rightarrow u = \sqrt{\frac{7}{2}gr}$
